title: Retarget the registration test whose premise the open role set removed
action: FIX-FIRST for a red THIS FEATURE CAUSED, unlike the earlier two which were pre-existing. verbs::drivers::tests::a_registration_failure_never_unwinds_the_standing_claim at drivers/tests.rs:2496 is red: it made a worker registration fail by passing the role name bogus, and sibling commit 81e7a4b4 (mrs-16) retired the worker registry's closed three-value enum, so bogus is now a perfectly legal role name and the test's premise is gone. mrs-17 found it and correctly left it alone — the file was neither in its cell nor reserved by it. The behavior the test guards is REAL and must keep its pin: a registration failure must never unwind a claim that is already standing. So find a registration failure that still exists after the open role set — a blank role, or whatever the shared worker_role_value shape check in verbs/state_group/workers.rs now refuses — and drive the test with that instead. Do NOT delete the test, and do NOT weaken it to assert something smaller; the claim-unwind guarantee is the point, the role name was only ever the trigger. If NO registration failure remains reachable, that is itself a finding: say so on the cap, because it would mean the guarantee is now untestable through this door rather than merely differently triggered. Run your verify with --no-fail-fast; the repo's declared command lacks it and aborts at the first failing target, so without it you may never reach your own test.
verify: PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --no-fail-fast --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --bin bee -- verbs::drivers

truths: The claim-unwind guarantee is still pinned by a test that actually fails when the guarantee is broken
The trigger is a registration failure that is reachable under the open role set
The test is neither deleted nor narrowed; if the guarantee became untestable through this door, the cap says so plainly

trace.outcome: Retarget the claim-unwind pin to a blank-role registration failure and prove it by mutation
deviations: Mutation check needed a temporary edit to verbs/drivers/prepare.rs (not a cell file): reserved it under mrs-w18 first, made the failure path unclaim the cell, confirmed the test goes red, then git checkout -- reverted it to pristine. The committed diff touches tests.rs only.

FINDING: the pre-existing assertions would NOT have caught a claim unwind. They read status off the Value returned by claim_and_reserve_for_dispatch, which is the pre-registration in-memory copy and still says claimed even when the store was unwound. Under the mutation the first assert passed and only the new on-disk read failed. The guarantee was nominally pinned but actually unpinned before this cell.

Also corrected a stale doc comment on the sibling test dispatch_prepare_claim_payload_pins_worker_registered_true, which still named an invalid cell tier as the one deterministic registration failure.
